_source: Jagatjit Agri Engineering Limited DRHP dated 25-Sep-2026 (SEBI filing 01-Oct-2026). Rs crore = Rs million / 10. Page cites are printed DRHP page numbers. FY26 is restated CONSOLIDATED and includes the two promoter proprietorships (SMW I and II) acquired w.e.f. 01-Apr-2025; FY25 and FY24 are restated STANDALONE of the pre-acquisition company, so the three years are not like-for-like. The DRHP's proforma FY25/FY24 (pp. 90-92, 158) is the like-for-like series. No stub period.

basis.name: Jagatjit Agri Engineering Limited
basis.outside: merchant-banker section only (named secondary sources, unverified); issuer analysis is from the DRHP

cites.rpt_s: pp. 94-95 (incl. promoter proprietorships SMW I/II in FY24-FY25; intra-group in FY26)
cites.cl: p. 93 (income tax 0.18 + GST 22.67 + other 6.50 + bank guarantees 42.35)
cites.reval: pp. 85-86; p. 107 (no shares issued out of revaluation reserve)

1.finding: 22:1 bonus (board 27-May-2026) and 1:2 split (EGM 04-May-2026) are applied retrospectively: EPS 5.64 / 1.42 / 0.57 and NAV 12.75 / 1.54 / 0.12 are on the restated count. The share count behind each year differs: FY26 uses 55,650,984 shares (313.90 / 5.64), FY25 and FY24 use about 46.1 m and 43.9 m (the pre-allotment count), because 9,650,984 shares were issued to the promoters on 22-Oct-2025 for the business transfer. FY26 EPS divides by the full post-issue count, not a time-weighted count; we have not re-weighted it.

2.finding: Cash flow statement is present. CFO 12.49 / 13.02 / 2.69 Rs cr (FY24 / FY25 / FY26); cumulative CFO/PAT 69.7% (281.93 / 404.39 Rs m), FY26 alone 8.6%. Cash generated from operations was Rs 131.36 m before Rs 104.52 m tax. FY26 working capital absorbed inventory Rs 445.46 m and other assets Rs 281.35 m. The FY26 receivables line shows a Rs 242.66 m decrease although closing receivables (Rs 612.95 m) exceed the FY25 standalone balance (Rs 244.72 m); the acquired opening balances are not shown separately in the statement.

3.finding: Current tax Rs 130.30 m of a Rs 130.21 m FY26 charge (deferred credit Rs 0.09 m). Cumulative current tax is 26.1% of cumulative PBT (147.09 / 562.64 Rs m) against a 25.17% statutory rate, so profit is struck after tax that has been paid.

4.finding: No related-party capex in FY26 (last: Rs 2.60 m from Goodfield Technology in FY24). Two other related-party points: (i) the Dehlon site for the Rs 716.64 m capex object is leased to the company by promoter Jagatjit Singh (rent Rs 1.01 m in FY26); (ii) Rs 45.00 m of loans/advances to Jagatjit Singh were outstanding at 31-Mar-2026 and Rs 10.00 m was advanced to Dharam Singh in FY26 (p. 95). The subsidiary Jagatjit Energies was bought for Rs 0.1 m on 30-Dec-2025 and receives no proceeds under the objects.

5.finding: Fresh issue is amount-based (Rs 3,000 m) with no fixed share count, so no price floor can be set. Specific objects total Rs 2,001.64 m (working capital 1,100.00; Dehlon capex 716.64; debt repayment 185.00) = 66.7% of gross proceeds. The other Rs 998.36 m must cover offer expenses and general corporate purposes; the stated GCP ceiling is 25% of gross proceeds (Rs 750 m), which would leave at least Rs 248.36 m for offer expenses if GCP were taken to the ceiling.

6.finding: No revaluation reserve in other equity; the company states it has not issued shares out of revaluation reserve.

7.finding: Goodwill Rs 4.55 m (0.6% of equity) in the restated consolidated balance sheet. The proforma balance sheet shows goodwill of Rs 65.66 m at FY25 and a capital reserve of Rs 32.98 m at FY24, so the purchase-accounting treatment differs between the restated and proforma statements; the DRHP does not reconcile them.

8.finding: Threshold test (above 80%): Northern and Central states were 93.99% of FY26 revenue (Punjab 25.79%, Haryana 18.48%, p. 56). Top customer Seth Agro Industries 25.21% of FY26 revenue (17.20% in FY25); top-10 customers 50.04%. Super Seeder and Straw Reaper together 59.06% of FY26 revenue (p. 26). Supplier concentration is disclosed only for FY25 and FY24 (top-1 was the promoter proprietorship SMW II at 52.55% and 44.13% of expenses), not for FY26; the DRHP says no long-term supply agreement terms are disclosed in the table.

9.finding: Contingent liabilities Rs 71.70 m (income tax 0.18; GST 22.67, of which Rs 2.14 m relates to SMW I and is to be borne by the company under the BTA; other 6.50; bank guarantees 42.35) = 10.1% of equity of Rs 709.29 m.

R1.finding: No qualification on the numbers. Auditor history: Singla Gupta & Co resigned 23-Apr-2024 (stated reason: preoccupation); Kansal Sandeep & Associates was appointed 02-May-2024 for FY24 only and ceased 30-Sep-2024 on completion of tenure; Anup Kumar Jain & Co appointed 30-Sep-2024 (peer review certificate 016161; the two earlier firms are shown without one). FY25 and FY24 statements are special-purpose Ind AS statements restated under ICDR. Promoters Jagatjit Singh and Dharam Singh were disqualified as directors 01-Nov-2016 to 31-Oct-2021 (a former group company struck off); a compounding application is pending (p. 36).

R2.finding: CARO / Rule 11(g): the accounting software had no database-level audit trail up to 31-Dec-2025 (FY26) and for all of FY25; the company says it was enabled in January 2026. No adjustment to the restated numbers.

R3.finding: Monitoring agency to be appointed (issue above Rs 1,000 m). Rs 185 m of proceeds repays bank borrowings of Rs 1,641.44 m outstanding at 31-Aug-2026; Rs 1,340.89 m is secured by promoters' personal guarantees (p. 40), so repayment may release some of them: an indirect promoter benefit. The related-party loans from promoters (Rs 2.29 m + 0.89 m + 4.83 m) are not listed for repayment.

R4.finding: Re-performed: the issuer states it does not meet Reg 6(1)(a) or 6(1)(c) and offers under Reg 6(2) (at least 75% to QIBs). Net tangible assets 704.75 / 70.78 / 5.32 Rs m and monetary assets 161.59 / 39.14 / 33.26 Rs m (22.9% / 55.3% / 625% of NTA) at FY26 / FY25 / FY24: the FY24 net worth of Rs 5.32 m is below the Rs 10 m test and FY25 monetary assets exceed 50%. The statement reproduces from the balance sheets. KPI EBITDA 557.38 reproduces from the P&L (444.12 + 101.63 + 46.66 - 35.03).

R5.finding: Offer for sale up to 3,100,000 shares by Jagatjit Singh, 6.3% of his 48,990,736 shares (below half of his holding). At the Rs 131.69 reference the OFS is Rs 408.2 m, 12.0% of a Rs 3,408.2 m offer (under the 20% ceiling). Re-test at the RHP price.

R6.finding: The DRHP lists only two IPOs handled by Keynote Financial Services in the period: Amir Chand Jagdish Kumar (Exports), Apr-2026, -23.53% at day 30 and -15.98% at day 90 against issue price; CSM Technologies, Jul-2026, -2.75% at day 30. Neither has a 180-day reading. Both are in data/merchant_bankers.json. The full BRLM track record is delegated to the BRLM's website.

R7.finding: Objects are funded from the fresh issue; the Rs 716.64 m capex has no orders placed (100% of cost, pp. 129, 139). Any means-of-finance tie-up beyond net proceeds is not described.

rationale.g1: Like-for-like growth: proforma revenue Rs 2,074.48 m (FY24) to 2,537.60 m (FY25, +22.3%) to Rs 4,139.70 m (FY26, +63.1%) (p. 158). Industry: CARE puts soil-preparation and cultivation equipment at a 10.2% CAGR FY26-FY30 and the tractor market at 7.5% (CARE report, issuer-commissioned, pp. 208-209). Bear assumes growth near the industry rate after a 63% step-up (the FY26 jump includes a Rs 1,043.46 m, 25.21% customer, p. 261, and subsidy-linked demand, p. 56); Bull assumes the 20-state distribution (20 states vs 15, p. 158) keeps compounding.
rationale.m: EBITDA margin 9.74% / 14.51% proforma FY24 / FY25 and 13.46% restated FY26 (p. 158); listed peers 13.27% (VST), 13.20% (Indo Farm), 13.17% (Escorts Kubota) in FY26 (p. 161). FY26 gross margin rose to 39.06% (proforma FY25 37.19%) but EBITDA margin fell 105 bp because commission (Rs 151.23 m), contract labour (Rs 172.45 m) and travel (Rs 80.77 m) grew with the direct-selling model (pp. 474-475). Bear sits below the FY26 level; Bull holds the proforma FY25 level.
rationale.nwc: Net working capital on the issuer's own table: Rs 1,029.46 m = 24.9% of FY26 revenue and Rs 658.57 m = 26.0% of proforma FY25 revenue (pp. 126, 158). Inventory days 132 (FY26) against 130 assumed in the issuer's plan; receivable days 45; payable days 106 falling to 95 (p. 128). Bear stays above FY26; Bull assumes the inventory build reverses toward 22%.
rationale.roic: Issuer-defined ROCE 31.10% FY26 and 35.59% FY25 (p. 158), but on a base that was small before the Rs 324.57 m business transfer; listed peers show ROCE of 13.28% (VST), 6.57% (Indo Farm), 11.10% (Escorts Kubota) (p. 161). Terminal ROIC is set from the top of the peer range (Bear 12%) to about three-quarters of the issuer's own FY26 figure (Bull 24%).

peers: Closest model among the three named: tillers and tractors for the same farm end-market; larger and branded, with net cash (net debt derived by us from the DRHP's EV/EBITDA, p. 156)
Tractors and cranes, similar size to the issuer; DRHP-named peer (p. 156); net debt derived by us from EV/EBITDA
Large tractor and construction-equipment OEM, about 28x the issuer's revenue; shown for reference, excluded; net debt derived by us
